findings.lens: Anabaptist / Mennonite (Schleitheim Confession, Confession of Faith in a Mennonite Perspective 1995)
findings.claim: Fairness to the other side: the history gives the tradition pole four entries (Vincent, Trent, Newman, Dei Verbum) and the Scripture-alone pole one (Westminster 1646).
findings.evidence: The obvious missing right-pole entry is Luther at Worms, 18 April 1521 ('unless I am convinced by Scripture and plain reason... my conscience is captive to the Word of God'), which is also where statement 14's 'bind the conscience' language comes from.
findings.fix: Insert before the Westminster line: '1521 — Luther at Worms: unless convinced by Scripture and plain reason, he will not recant; conscience is bound to the Word of God.'

findings.lens: Anglican (broad, Thirty-Nine Articles / Book of Common Prayer)
findings.claim: The history jumps from Trent (1546) to Westminster (1646) and skips the settlement that defines the middle of this axis: Article VI (1571) and Hooker (1594).
findings.evidence: Article VI, 'Holy Scripture containeth all things necessary to salvation', is the classic statement of sufficiency-without-biblicism; Hooker's Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity (1594-97) is the standard defence of Scripture read with reason and the church's tradition, and is cited by both Catholics and Protestants as the via media text.
findings.fix: Insert before the Westminster entry: '1571-1594: The Thirty-Nine Articles make Scripture the test of what may be required as necessary to salvation; Hooker's Laws defends the church's authority in what Scripture leaves open.'

findings.claim: The Tradition timeline gives the 'with tradition' pole four entries (Vincent 434, Trent 1546, Newman 1845, Dei Verbum 1965) and the 'Scripture alone' pole one (Westminster 1646); a reader on the right sees his side's history as a single line between two Catholic councils.
findings.evidence: Count of history entries by pole: 4 to 1. The two obvious right-pole landmarks are missing: Worms 1521 and the American restoration plea of 1809.
findings.fix: Add '1521 Diet of Worms: Luther will not recant unless convinced by Scripture and plain reason' and '1809 Thomas Campbell's Declaration and Address launches the Restoration plea: no creed as a test of fellowship, "where the Scriptures speak, we speak; where the Scriptures are silent, we are silent."'

findings.lens: confessional Lutheran (LCMS / WELS / Book of Concord)
findings.claim: The Protestant slot in the Tradition history is given to Westminster (1646) alone; the two Lutheran sola Scriptura moments, Worms (1521) and the Formula of Concord's Rule and Norm (1577), which coined the judge/witness distinction the whole axis turns on, are absent.
findings.evidence: Luther at Worms, 1521: "unless I am convinced by Scripture and plain reason... popes and councils have often erred"; FC Ep Rule and Norm 1-8 (1577) predates WCF ch. 1 by seventy years and is its direct model for "Scripture alone is judge".
findings.fix: Insert before the Westminster entry: {"when": "1577", "what": "Formula of Concord, Rule and Norm: Scripture alone is judge; creeds and confessions are witnesses to be judged by it, not judges themselves."} (optionally also {"when": "1521", "what": "Luther at Worms: conscience bound by Scripture, since popes and councils have erred."})

findings.lens: Reformed charismatic (John Piper, Wayne Grudem, Sam Storms, Sovereign Grace Churches, Acts 29 continuationists)
findings.claim: The Tradition history is four entries for the tradition pole (Vincent, Trent, Newman, Dei Verbum) against one for Scripture alone (Westminster).
findings.evidence: history array: 434 Vincent, 1546 Trent, 1646 WCF, 1845 Newman, 1965 Dei Verbum. The intro promises 'both sides of every axis get a fair hearing'. The defining Scripture-alone moment is Luther at Worms, 1521, and the 1521 gap is also what makes the 1546 Trent line read as unprovoked.
findings.fix: Insert before the 1646 entry: {"when": "1521", "what": "Luther at Worms refuses to recant unless convinced by Scripture and plain reason: his conscience is captive to the Word of God."}
